title: Night Desk
protagonist: her, nineteen, three weeks at the Wayside
note: Authored from games/night_desk/sheets/ as a test of the REVIEW FORMAT, not of game design. The sheets were signed off before any TOML existed; every disagreement between them and this build is recorded in iterations/001/BUILD_VS_SHEET.md.

want.who_she_is: Nineteen, three weeks at the Wayside — twelve rooms on a state highway forty minutes from anywhere. She works the desk from ten at night and sleeps in room twelve, and eighty dollars a week comes back out of her pay for it. WHAT SHE HAS TO LOSE: the room, which is the same man as the job.
want.appetite: To be seen, and then to be seen doing more than being seen. It cannot complete: corruption opens exhibitionism, exhibitionism costs corruption, and the ceiling on each is the other one.
want.ascent: BOTTOM: the counter between her and whoever is on the other side of it. TOP: her own hours, the monitor watched rather than checked, and both men asking for things she decides about rather than refuses.
want.charge_note: Decision 10. She cannot leave — $400 against $60 — and the building is seven rooms. The change has to happen where she already is, which is what makes every rung a decision rather than an escape.

map.shape: One building and the ground it stands on. the_lot is the exterior and the root; the desk sits on it and everything else hangs off the desk; room_6 hangs off the corridor.
map.note: ⚠️ RE-ROOTED 2026-08-31. The sheets had the desk as root with the lot as one of five exits — an exterior leaf, which the-map.md R3 forbids and gate 28 catches. The sheets were wrong against a rule the skill already held; the place-sheet format has no row for how a room attaches to the map, which is why nothing caught it.
